summary: Completed comprehensive testing of Account Settings feature for MicLocker marketplace. All 18 backend API tests passed (100%). Frontend E2E tests completed successfully - Account Settings page loads correctly with Username, Email, and Password change forms working as expected.

minor.issue: Returns 403 instead of 401 for unauthenticated requests - minor inconsistency but acceptable

passed_tests: POST /api/auth/account/change-username - wrong password returns 401 with 'Incorrect password'
POST /api/auth/account/change-username - same username returns 400 with 'different from current'
POST /api/auth/account/change-email/request - success returns 200 and sends verification code
Full email change flow: request -> get code -> verify -> email updated in profile
Login with new password works after password change
Frontend: Account Settings link visible in user dropdown menu
Frontend: Account Settings page loads with data-testid='account-settings-page'
Frontend: Username section with Change button and form fields
Frontend: Email section with Change button and verification code flow
Frontend: Password section with Change button, current/new/confirm fields
Frontend: Security warning about logout after password change visible
critical_code_review_comments: Account settings implementation is correct and secure
All credential changes require password verification - good security practice
Email change uses 2-step verification (password + email code) - secure
Password change correctly logs user out for security
Validation messages are clear and helpful
data-testid attributes properly implemented for all form elements

success_rate.frontend: 100% (All UI elements and forms working correctly)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Account Settings feature is fully implemented and working. Users can change username (requires password), email (requires password + verification code to new email), and password (requires current password, logs out after change). All endpoints require authentication via Bearer token. Verification codes are logged in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log when SES email fails (sandbox mode). The Account Settings page is accessible via /account or /account/settings routes, and via the user dropdown menu 'Account Settings' link.
